pageCache.text:
Headteachers Welcome
Welcome to Wyvern St Edmund’s Academy
Naturally, the education of your child is extremely important to you — and it is to us as well. At Wyvern St Edmund’s, “being the best you can be” reflects our commitment to nurturing every young person academically, personally and spiritually, so that they can fulfil their potential, enjoy school life and be well prepared for life beyond the classroom. Inspired by Matthew 5:16 - "Let your light shine" — we encourage every student to grow in confidence, character and ambition.
Wyvern St Edmund’s is a popular coeducational secondary school set within extensive and beautiful grounds on the eastern edge of Salisbury. Our campus overlooks Laverstock Downs, with views towards Salisbury Cathedral, creating a calm and inspiring environment in which young people can learn and thrive. We offer students a wide range of exciting opportunities, both within and beyond the classroom, supported by strong specialist facilities.
Our dedicated and highly skilled staff work together to inspire, challenge and nurture our students. We have high expectations for all and aim to deliver an education that enables young people to achieve academic excellence, develop their individual talents and grow into confident, compassionate individuals with the skills and attitudes needed to succeed.
As a Church of England Academy, our values shape everything we do. We work as a community to fulfil our shared vision — helping every student to work hard, aim high, be kind and serve others. Central to this is our belief in the importance of a strong partnership between school, students and parents. We know that when we work together, young people are best supported to flourish.
We hope our website provides the information you are looking for and gives you a sense of what makes Wyvern St Edmund’s special. Please do not hesitate to contact us via the main reception if you need any further assistance. We look forward to welcoming you to our academy in the near future.
Bruce Burley, Headteacher

pageCache.text:
British Values at WSE
At the heart of our approach to British Values at WSE is the aim to equip our students with the knowledge, skills, and attitudes they need to be able to function in a diverse society. This is underpinned by our school vision in that we encourage our students to strive to be the best version of themselves which can be achieved through responsible citizenship and service to others and their communities.
All schools are required by law to promote the fundamental British values of: democracy, the rule of law and individual liberty.
We are required to ensure students should understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
What are ‘fundamental British values’?
Schools are required to provide for the spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development of their students. As part of this requirement, schools are expected to actively promote fundamental British values.
The government defines these as:
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty
What does this mean for my child?
Our programme for learning about fundamental British values is designed to prepare children and young people for life in modern Britain. This includes helping students understand:
the importance of combatting discrimination
What does this look like at WSE?
Frequently Asked Questions
Absolutely. One of the fundamental British values is respect and tolerance of people with different faiths and of no faith. This is in line with Church of England’s inclusive vision for education. British law protects people’s freedom to hold their own beliefs. Any prejudice or discrimination towards students, on the basis of their faith, goes against the fundamental British Values and will not be tolerated.
The curriculum provides lots of opportunities to look at fundamental British Values. Your child will have experience of this in lessons such as religious education (RS) and personal, social and health education (PSHE).
Promoting fundamental British Values reinforces and compliments, not changes, our ethos.

pageCache.pageTitle: WSE: A Church of England Academy - Wyvern St Edmund's
pageCache.text:
WSE: A Church of England Academy
"Be the best you can be" - build your legacy!
At WSE we believe that we are all known to God and made in the image of God meaning we are each valued as individuals blessed with a God given talent. Therefore, we each have the potential to make a unique contribution as stewards of God’s Grace. We seek to help our students find their gift and in doing so understand how they can use it in order to serve their local, national and global communities and be the change makers of the future.
Wyvern St Edmund's Academy opened as one academy in September 2022. In 2018 Wyvern College and St Edmund’s Girl's School became a colocated school and developed into a single mixed secondary school. Both schools were foundation Church schools and have a long heritage of leadership guided by strong Christian values. We have a long standing and strong relationship with the Diocese of Salisbury. Both schools are founder members of the Magna Learning Partnership Trust of Schools. The MLP is committed to upholding the Christian characteristics of the Church schools in the Trust. The Trust vision is:
‘Let your light shine’ Matthew 5:16.
The colocation of the two schools in 2018 was a clear expression of the Christian principles of both the Trust and the two schools to ensure that all students receive a broad and balanced curriculum in a co-educational setting. We ensure that they leave as well-rounded individuals prepared for life in the 21st century, with the ambition to make a positive contribution in service of their community and the world beyond.
As Church of England Schools our ethos is underpinned by Christian values and principles and embraces the Church of England vision for young people, a vision of ‘human flourishing for all’,of a life lived in all its fullness (John 10:10). It is inclusive for those of all faith and of none, serving the common good of all our community.
Our Christian values (rooted in biblical teachings, see below) and the theological underpinning (Matthew 5:16) of our vision provide the foundation for all our decisions, they are evident in all our interactions and shape the daily life our school community.
We are committed to the personal, moral, and spiritual development of our students to enable them to become independent and self-motivated; responsible for themselves and others and prepared to work for the common good.
At the heart of this commitment is that every member of our school community is this belief that we are all known to and valued by God. Therefore, we aim to ensure that every member of our school community knows they are valued and respected in the knowledge we all have the capacity to make a unique contribution.
WSE Spirituality Statement
Wyvern St Edmund’s is committed to being a community which promotes spiritual development. Spirituality looks outwards to reflect on the natural world, the environment and human capacities and achievement. It looks inwards to reflect on beliefs, values, feelings, hopes, dreams, ideals and aspirations. This reflection shapes the way we think, and feel about creation, ourselves, and other people, and how we respond.
The promise by Jesus of ‘life in all its fullness’ lies at the heart of Christian Spirituality and results in human flourishing. Christian Spirituality reflects the teachings of the Bible and involves the whole life of a person responding to God’s love. As a Church Academy, we are committed to giving students opportunities to explore and reflect on religious faith and particularly the Christian faith.
Our Christian values of work hard, aim high, be kind and serve others will deepen as we develop our spirituality within the life of the Academy.
Our commitment to our young people in a Church of England Academy:
As educators in a Church Academy, we take seriously our responsibility to uphold the core Church of England principles of wisdom, dignity, hope and community.
Our teachers are committed to these principles through:
Our Core Values are rooted in biblical teaching:
Work hard to acheive more!
Give your best in everything you do. Learning takes effort, and success comes from perseverance.
“Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord” (Colossians 3:23).
Set ambitious goals and believe you can achieve them. Don’t settle for less than your potential.
“I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me” (Philippians 4:13).
Be kind and connect!
Treat everyone with respect and compassion. Kindness builds community and reflects God’s love.
“Be kind and compassionate to one another” (Ephesians 4:32).
Serve others to make a difference!
Be an active part of school life, and an advocate for others. Contribute, collaborate, and celebrate shared success.
“Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11).

pageCache.text:
Curriculum by Subjects
Subjects Studied in Years 7 - 9
At Key Stage Three, students study the traditional academic subjects: Maths, English, Science, Languages and Humanities (Geography, History and RS) and alongside these we offer a healthy mixture of Arts and Technology subjects. PE (including Dance), Drama, and Music are taught as distinct subjects and students follow a carousel of Technology lessons enabling them to study Food and Nutrition, Textiles and Product Design throughout the year. The Year 7 curriculum also offers the teaching of Mindfulness by qualified practitioners, equipping students with techniques to maintain good mental health. Personal, Social, Health and Economic education (PSHE) is taught to all KS3 students and covers important topics that support our students in becoming good, responsible citizens.
Subjects Studied in Years 10 and 11
Key Stage 4 students all continue their study of the traditional academic subjects at GCSE: Maths, English and Science and one other traditional subject (e.g. History, Geography, Modern Foreign Languages or Computer Science). As a Church of England Academy, all students also study RS GCSE and continue to participate in core PE and PSHE to ensure that good physical and mental health is prioritised.
Whilst we believe that studying a language at GCSE is an excellent choice, we do not insist that students do so, because it is not the right choice for all. However, we do aim to meet the government target of 75% of students achieving the EBacc qualification, but as a result of students choosing to do so because they enjoy their language learning and see its value in life.
Students also have two other free choices to make from a wide range of Arts, Design and Technology and contemporary subjects.
For some students, this programme of study is not appropriate for their educational needs so we create a personalised GCSE package that is more suitable for ensuring their success at Key Stage Four.
For those students who feel limited by the choices they have to make at GCSE, we ensure that they can continue to develop their passions and interests by way of our excellent after-school enrichment programme (see co-curriculum).
Business StudiesChild DevelopmentComputer ScienceDanceDramaDTEnglishFrenchGeographyGermanHistoryMathsMusicPEPSHCEScienceSpanish
WSE Curriculum Hours Overview 2025-26
WSE employs five one-hour lessons per day plus a half hour tutorial slot with their tutor. The timetable runs over 2 weeks giving each student 50 hours of curriculum time per fortnight.

KS4 (Y10-11) - Hours per subject per fortnight
In KS4 a mixture of GCSEs and vocational qualifications are offered. This list is subject to changes each year.
Remote Learning
In the event of a school closure preventing in-person attendance, we are committed to ensuring the continuity of education through remote learning; work will be provided via Class Charts. All students have a 100% booklet and a self-quizzing book - we recommend that students complete self-quizzing if they are not able to access the work set on Class Charts.
In individual circumstances where a student is unable to attend school but is able to learn (e.g. recovering from an operation or from injuries where attendance might inhibit recovery), a discussion will take place with the attendance team to confirm remote learning options. They will include:
Using the 100% booklet to self-quiz.
The Right to Withdraw from Religious Education
Any parent has a right to withdraw their child from Religious Education (RE). If a parent asks for their child to be wholly, or partly, excused from attending any RE at the school, the school must comply unless the request is withdrawn. The school remains responsible for the supervision of any child withdrawn from RE, unless the child is lawfully receiving Religious Education elsewhere. Parents do not need to explain their reasons for seeing withdrawal.
If a parent is wishing to withdraw their child from RE it is kindly requested that they contact the headteacher directly. It is helpful to know the religious issues leading to the request and the practical implications of withdrawal.

pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
We are committed to working together with all members of our school community and believe in providing every possible opportunity to develop the full potential of all our students. The SEND team aim to ensure that students with SEND are able to learn and progress, despite any challenges they might face. Getting to know the student’s strengths and areas of need is integral to the work we do. We work closely with tutors, teachers, parents/carers and the students themselves to develop an understanding of the young person and how best to support them.
All students have the right to a broad and balanced curriculum including extra-curricular activities, to feel valued and have their self-esteem promoted.
The people to contact this year with regard to any SEND queries are:
Miss S Hunter – SENDCo (Special Educational Needs and Disability Co-ordinator)
Email: senco@wyvernsteds.org
Nathalie Allexant-Rowland – SEND Governor
We also employ 15 teaching assistants (TAs) who specialise in identified curriculum areas and whose work is primarily in the classroom, working alongside the class teacher in the delivery of teaching and learning. They also deliver the interventions as outlined in the SEND Information and Policy by our SENDCo. and mentor students who require a more in depth level of monitoring.
In addition to this, we work closely with our Pastoral Support Team.
For more information please see 'Support for wellbeing at WSE'
Please see our Policies & Documents page for the SEND Information Report

pageCache.text:
Young Carers
Please fine contact details below for our Young Carers Champion and Young Carers SLT Link:
Ms Nat Clark (Young Carer Champion): wseyoungcarers@wyvernsteds.org Mr D Hill (SLT Link): dhill@wyvernsteds.org
What is a Young Carer?
A young carer is a child, under the age of 18, who spends time looking after or helping a family or household member or members. The person may require support from a young carer for a range of reasons, including physical or mental illnesses, disability or due to the misuse of alcohol or substances. Most young carers look after a parent or a sibling but can be caring for more than one person, for example, a parent and a sibling. A young carer carries out a significant role within their home.
The range of care, and time spent caring, can vary, but every young carer carefully balances their schoolwork and social life. Without recognition and support, caring responsibilities can have far-reaching impact on a child’s life. No two young carers’ needs are the same, which is why WSE offer various support and initiatives to meet the needs of young carers.
At WSE we provide a weekly young carer breakfast club – a safe space where breakfast is provided and a time to chat with other young carers and be part of student voice helping to continue to develop our young carer provision. We can also offer extra help with homework, flexibility around calling home, someone to talk to and alternatives to after school activities. We can also make a referral to Wiltshire Council for a Young Carer Assessment with your permission. We work closely with MyTime, the Young Carer charity and Wiltshire Young Carers in Schools to ensure our provision is informed and up to date.
If you believe that your child is a young carer but they are not yet registered as one, please let us know and we can discuss a referral for a Young Carers Assessment by Wiltshire Council.
You can also self-refer to young carers by contacting:
0300 456 0108 Integratedfrontdoor@wiltshire.gov.ukOnce a referral has been submitted, it will be allocated to a member of the Wiltshire Council Team, who will contact you to arrange a visit so that they can complete a holistic assessment. This will explore what support can be offered to your family.
If you have any questions or require further information about young carers, please contact:
wseyoungcarers@wyvernsteds.org
Useful Links for Local Young Carer Support
The following website provide valuable information about young carers in Wiltshire.
Young carers - Wiltshire Council – This website contains information on the young carers assessment with IFD to register them as a young carer, as well as information about youth action Wiltshire and the provision they offer.
Young Carer Voice- Wiltshire Council – This webpage provides information about the Young Carers Council and the Young Carer Magazine.
Youth Action Wiltshire | Wiltshire Young Carers Service – Youth Action Wiltshire are commissioned by Wiltshire Council to provide the Young Carers Service. They have young carer support workers for each Wiltshire region and offer fun breaks with other young carers. You can contact the service by emailing wiltshireyoungcarers@youthactionwiltshire.org.
Young Adult Carers - Carers Together Wiltshire – This website is for young adult carers (over 16s), offering support with college and the transition.
Young Carers - Forward Carers – Forward carers provide a website for Wiltshire's digital offer for unpaid carers of all ages. They can also provide young carers with an ID card. To sign up for a Young Carers ID Card Carer ID Card - Wiltshire Carers.

pageCache.text:
Careers Programme Information
At WSE, careers education is an integral part of our wider Personal Development programme. We want every student to develop the knowledge, skills, confidence and experiences they need to make informed and ambitious decisions about their future.
Careers at WSE
The world of education, training and employment is constantly changing. New technologies, emerging industries and changes in the labour market mean that young people have more opportunities available to them than ever before; but navigating those choices can also be challenging.
Our careers programme helps students understand themselves, explore the opportunities available to them and develop the Future Skills they will need for their next steps and beyond. We encourage students to be ambitious, challenge stereotypes and consider pathways and careers they may not previously have encountered.
Careers education begins in Year 7 and develops progressively throughout each student's time at WSE. Through curriculum learning, employer encounters, experiences of workplaces, engagement with further and higher education, labour market information and personal guidance, students build the knowledge and confidence to make informed decisions about their future.
We are committed to ensuring that careers guidance is inclusive and responsive to the needs of every student. Students are supported at key transition points and have access to impartial information about the full range of pathways available, including sixth form, further education, apprenticeships, technical education and employment.
Our careers programme is developed in partnership with students, parents and carers, employers, education and training providers and our wider community, helping students connect their learning in school with the opportunities available beyond it.
What students experience:
From Year 7 to Year 11, students follow a progressive careers programme that supports them to understand themselves, explore different careers and pathways, develop their Future Skills and make informed decisions about their next steps.
Students experience careers through curriculum learning, employer encounters, workplace experiences, further and higher education encounters, careers events and personal guidance. As they progress through school, they are supported at key decision points, including GCSE options and post-16 choices.
All students have access to Unifrog throughout their time at WSE, providing a central platform to explore careers, courses, apprenticeships and pathways, record their experiences and skills, and support their future applications.
Explore Our Careers Learning Journey:
The Gatsby Benchmarks: ensuring high-quality careers provision
The eight Gatsby Benchmarks define world-class careers guidance for young people in England and provide the framework through which we plan, evaluate and continually develop our careers provision.
Following an extensive review of evidence and practice, the Gatsby Benchmarks were updated for implementation from the 2025–26 academic year. The updated Benchmarks retain the original eight areas while strengthening the focus on careers as a whole-school priority, inclusion and the needs of every young person, meaningful encounters and experiences, the effective use of information and data, and engagement with parents and carers.
At WSE, the Gatsby Benchmarks are embedded within our careers programme and form an important part of our wider Personal Development provision. We use the Benchmarks alongside statutory careers guidance to ensure that all students benefit from a coherent, progressive and high-quality careers programme.
We regularly evaluate our provision against all eight Benchmarks and use this evaluation, alongside feedback from students, parents and carers, staff, employers and education providers, to identify strengths and priorities for continued development.
The eight Gatsby Benchmarks are:
Together, the Gatsby Benchmarks help us ensure that careers education at WSE is not a series of standalone activities, but a planned and progressive programme that supports every student to understand their options, develop their aspirations and prepare for their next steps.

Every Day is an Open Day at WSE
Choosing the right secondary school is an important decision and we believe the best way to get to know WSE is to see our school as it really is on a normal school day. That’s why we’re opening our doors for school tours every day from Monday 28th September 2026.
Tours will take place during the school day and will be led by our Student Guides. These personalised tours will give families the opportunity to: see lessons, experience the atmosphere around school, hear directly from our students about what life at WSE is really like and meet our headteacher or another member of the senior team.
We know that families of children currently in Year 6 are making important decisions about secondary school applications; Year 6 families will be given priority booking for tours before October half term. Following half term, we will open bookings to Year 5 families, giving them an early opportunity to start exploring their secondary school options. We also welcome visits from any other prospective families, local community members or potential staff members who want to see the school in action.
Every day is an open day.

KS4 Courses
As of Oct 2026 - For Year 10 in Sept 2027.
Due to sweeping reforms from the Department for Education and Ofsted, there will be changes this year to the options process. We will put more information on here explaining our options process once these national changes have been confirmed.
Below is the options process that current Y10 (Sept 2026) have undergone.
The options process for Y10 and 11 starts early in the spring term of Y9. Students and their parents are invited to an options evening where teachers give information about the courses on offer.
Students also receive a detailed booklet of information about the courses and following the evening have a few weeks to read it carefully and make up their minds. We strongly encourage students to talk to their teachers during this ‘thinking time’ in order to make the best choice. We also ask students to choose a back-up option, as it is not always possible to satisfy every student’s first choices.
We also see this process as a partnership, and we may well encourage students to consider certain options, such as a language, as we can see that this may well be of benefit to them later, even when they might not see things the same way.
Some courses, such as GCSE Computer Science, GCSE PE or the Triple Science route will probably depend on the student achieving a certain minimum standard in their end of Year 9 assessments.
We aim to confirm these choices by Easter of each year.
List of courses available at KS4 (Y10-11)
We offer a mix of GCSEs and vocational qualifications.
In addition to the core offer of English, Maths, Science, RS, Core PE and PSHE students select 3 courses from the following list.

Intent
The curriculum at WSE actively sets out to develop learners into well-rounded citizens of the twenty first century who will embody the values we hold dear.
It is broad, balanced and exciting and offers the wide range of subjects that only a relatively large school can. The extensive learning opportunities provided by our curriculum enables our students to flourish and become the very best version of themselves.
We fulfil the statutory requirements placed on all schools and academies and use the National Curriculum as a foundation for all our curriculum planning. Through a three-year Key Stage 3, we fully equip our learners with the knowledge, skills and habits of learning needed to thrive during Key Stage 4. Department leaders plan sequences of learning that challenge all our learners; it is very important to us that students are thinking hard in lessons - irrespective of their starting point.
Students experience an extensive range of academic, creative and technical subjects, which are taught by highly qualified specialists. Additionally, we have a broad wider curriculum which helps students to understand themselves and the world around them. This includes: religious education; personal, social, health and economic education; sex and relationships education, and citizenship.
At WSE we also recognise the importance of developing students holistically beyond lesson time through a comprehensive range of enriching experiences, also known as the co-curriculum.
